items.title: The Matrix
items.line: The Matrix opened in the US on 31 March 1999. The Wachowskis shot it in Sydney on a $63 million budget, and it won four Oscars and made bullet time famous.

items.title: Napster
items.line: Napster launched in June 1999, built by Shawn Fanning and Sean Parker and named after Fanning's school nickname. It peaked at 26.4 million verified users in February 2001.

items.title: The Blair Witch Project
items.line: The Blair Witch Project premiered at Sundance on 23 January 1999 and opened wide on 30 July. Fake police reports on its website helped it gross $248.6 million.

items.title: The Phantom Menace
items.line: Star Wars: The Phantom Menace opened on 19 May 1999 on a $113.8 million budget. Critics aimed a lot of their complaints at Jar Jar Binks, played by Ahmed Best.

items.title: Dreamcast
items.line: Sega launched the Dreamcast in North America on 9 September 1999 at $199, and in Europe on 14 October. It sold 9.13 million and was discontinued on 31 March 2001.

items.title: The euro
items.line: On 1 January 1999 the euro began as an electronic currency in 11 countries. Notes and coins did not reach wallets until January 2002.

items.title: The Sopranos
items.line: The Sopranos premiered on HBO on 10 January 1999. David Chase's show ran 86 episodes until 2007 and won 21 Primetime Emmys.
